For a one–dimensional infinite square well the single–particle eigen-energies are  

E_n = n² E ,   with   E = π²ħ² /(2mL²),   n = 1,2,3 …

The four particles are identical fermions (spin ½), so the Pauli principle allows at most two particles (one with spin ↑, one with spin ↓) in each spatial level n.

Ground state (fill from the bottom up)
• n = 1 : 2 particles → energy 2·(1²E) = 2E  
• n = 2 : 2 particles → energy 2·(2²E) = 8E  
Total ground-state energy  = 2E + 8E = 10E

First excited state (make the smallest possible single excitation)
Move one particle from n = 2 to the next empty level n = 3:  
• n = 1 : 2 particles → 2E  
• n = 2 : 1 particle  → 4E  
• n = 3 : 1 particle  → 9E  
Total energy  = 2E + 4E + 9E = 15E

Second excited state (next smallest increase)
Either move one particle from n = 1 to n = 3 or interchange one n = 1 with n = 2 while moving the freed n = 2 particle to n = 3. The smallest energy above 15E obtained this way is

• n = 1 : 1 particle → 1E  
• n = 2 : 2 particles→ 8E  
• n = 3 : 1 particle → 9E  
Total energy  = 1E + 8E + 9E = 18E

Thus  
Ground state energy     = 10E  
First excited energy    = 15E  
Second excited energy   = 18E  

The list that matches these values is  

(D) 10E, 15E, 18E  

Answer: D
